overall: A dry, unhurried colleague tells you about a control room where a screen sees trouble before it arrives, plain and a little amused, with the facts doing the persuading. The read opens curious, drops to its quietest at the dropped model and the operator's honesty, and settles into a steady, owned close with no rise at the end.

lines.text: In a Port Arthur refinery control room, a screen is drawing a steam pressure dip that hasn't happened yet.
lines.intent: hook, a small impossible image set down plainly
lines.note: Weight on 'hasn't happened yet'. Say it matter of fact, as if it is a normal Tuesday, with no wink.

lines.text: The refinery belongs to TotalEnergies, in Jefferson County. It runs about 238,000 barrels of crude a day through 47 units.
lines.note: Level, informational. Weight on '238,000'. Land the figure flat with no lift on 'units'.

lines.text: One of them is the delayed coker. It uses high heat to crack heavy leftover oil into lighter, more valuable products.
lines.intent: explain the hero unit in one breath of plain language
lines.note: Weight on 'crack'. Friendly, like explaining to a neighbor. Say 'coker' as KOH-ker.

lines.text: The coker's turbines need high pressure steam, and it has to keep coming.
lines.intent: state the dependency, the stakes in miniature
lines.note: Weight on 'keep coming'. A touch firmer than the line before.

lines.text: When a boiler falters, steam line pressure dips. A dip can trip a compressor, and the plant can shut down and flare.
lines.intent: chain of consequence, the problem at full size
lines.note: Build through the chain, weight on 'trip' and then 'flare'. This is the loudest the read gets, still controlled.

lines.text: The console operator gets little time to decide which less critical equipment gives up its steam.
lines.intent: bring the person in, the squeeze on the decision
lines.note: Drop after the previous line. Weight on 'little time'. Sympathetic and even.

lines.text: So in October 2024, TotalEnergies began testing a Honeywell AI tool on the coker console.
lines.intent: turn from problem to the pilot
lines.note: Weight on 'testing'. A fresh start, light and forward. Say 'twenty twenty-four' naturally.

lines.text: Honeywell's early count, in November 2025, was five potential events, flagged an average of 12 minutes before an alarm.
lines.intent: first evidence, an early and modest number
lines.note: Weight on '12 minutes'. Keep 'five potential events' even and unimpressed. Let the figure speak.

lines.text: A later account said its models predicted pressure dips 10 to 18 minutes earlier than before. That is a runway of time to act.
lines.intent: the headline result, then its meaning
lines.note: Weight on '10 to 18'. Say the range cleanly. 'Runway of time to act' lands warm and plain, no sell.

lines.text: Minutes change the job. Operators acted on at least two of its alerts. Thomas Klein, in process control there, said it was the first time AI at the site caught a situation it had predicted.
lines.intent: payoff, proof it was used by real people
lines.note: Short opener, dry. Weight on 'acted' and again on 'first time'. Say Klein as KLINE. Attribution is reported speech, not drama.

lines.text: Not every model earned its place. One tried to predict the level in the coke drums. It was right 75 percent of the time and was still dropped, because drum switching depends on things outside the model.
lines.intent: the turn, honest about a failure
lines.note: Quietest stretch of the film. Weight on 'still dropped'. Deliver '75 percent' quietly after the louder lines so it is heard. Slight dry smile on 'earned its place'.

lines.text: Another tool turns past alarms on more than 300 coker tags into examples of what worked before. Klein said it gave new operators high value. It is still in evaluation, and he presented it at Honeywell's own user conference.
lines.intent: second tool, with the caveat stated straight
lines.note: Weight on 'high value', then lower and cooler on 'still in evaluation'. 'Honeywell's own' carries a faint dry edge.

lines.text: Klein admits he was pessimistic. Now he says AI has room on the console, but it is not plug and play, and it needs support.
lines.intent: the human admission, trust earned by candor
lines.note: Weight on 'pessimistic'. Warm and unguarded. Weight on 'needs support', unhurried.

lines.text: His advice is to bring operators in from the start. The gauge reads now. The screen reads next. The call is still the operator's.
lines.intent: button, land the idea and set it down
lines.note: Advice is plain. 'Now' and 'next' are a quiet pair, the second a shade lower. Final sentence is the heaviest and slowest, falling on 'operator's' with no lift.
